finding: The actual serialized physical dispatcher has qualified irrigation interval entry points. The ordinary production bootstrap owns private committed columns and has no public scheduled-management entry. A separate irrigation adapter cannot read these private accepted states or consume the actual crop/weather daystart without an explicit shared application hook.
proposed_contract: Add a bounded bootstrap entry preparing irrigation forcing from each internal committed state and immutable same-window owner weather/crop inputs. Reuse irrigation preparation, accepted CML and availability receipts; execute via existing run_standalone_with_forcing, publish management only for completed committed physical results. Retain existing per-column/multiswap transaction semantics. Joint continuation includes weather/crop daystart and irrigation event/weekly/allocation state.
held_fixed: existing ordinary bottom and optional-state profile admission checks
required_owner_action: Resolve and admit compatible crop1197 bootstrap/dispatcher postimages, then centrally admit the explicit management hook and preserved joint restart. Do not replay or overwrite an active owner candidate.
required_proofs: accepted root extent and hydraulic material-consistent FC/stress/wilting values
TCS2/3/4/6/7/8 and DCS1/limits through the actual application bootstrap
O0/O2 and affected existing application/crop/F-CI preservation
owner_reuse_rule: Rediscover these exact owner interfaces after admission and reuse them. The weather interval currently constructs effective forcing internally and exposes no irrigation-management input.
